body: We might as well just remove `GameStateSnapshotRef`, and replace it with `Ref<GameStateSnapshot>`, unless I'm missing something. It doesn't look like it serves any real purpose currently.

> We might as well just remove `GameStateSnapshotRef`, and replace it with `Ref<GameStateSnapshot>`, unless I'm missing something. It doesn't look like it serves any real purpose currently.

The comment says:
```
// A ref to a refcounted object which is a wrapper of a non-refcounted object.
```
So `GameStateSnapshot` would need to extend `RefCounted` instead of `Object`.
I haven't checked why it was implemented this way and whether there would be any drawback to reference counting `GameStateSnapshot`.

But yeah with this change it seems like we're just making `GameStateSnapshot` refcounted through a wrapper, so why not refcount it directly?

Yeah, I think `GameStateSnapshot` inheriting from `RefCounted` should be fine, updated with this change.  There was a comment: `// Ideally, this would extend EditorDebuggerRemoteObject and be refcounted, but we can't have it both ways.` - maybe it was originally meant to inherit from this class, but was changed to inherit from `Object` instead at some point.  I kept the `create_ref` method for calling code to use instead of using the constructor directly, since it has some error handling logic/returning null.

There is some code that uses raw pointers to `GameStateSnapshot` objects - now that the snapshots are being freed, there's some risk that these pointers could point to already deleted objects.  I think all of the `GameStateSnapshot *` uses in `modules/objectdb_profiler` are safe, but I ran into an interaction with `EditorInspector` that caused a crash (fixed with latest update):
- Create more than 10 snapshots (`ObjectDBProfilerPanel` has an `LRUCache` that stores 10 snapshots)
- With a snapshot selected, go to the "Classes" tab, and select a class and object
- Object should appear in the Inspector panel
- Scroll through/select 10 other snapshots
- After the original snapshot is removed from the `LRUCache`, `EditorInspector`'s `NOTIFICATION_PROCESS` logic will check to update its `EditorProperty`s
- `EditorProperty` checks if its `Object *` is not null, rather than checking `ObjectDB` for an `ObjectID`, so it sees a deleted object's memory as valid, and crashes on use

The above was only an issue if the currently edited object was part of the snapshot - if something else was selected later before the snapshot was freed, it wouldn't crash when going back through the inspector's history, since that path checks `ObjectID`.  To fix this issue, I added a check before freeing the snapshots, to clear the inspector if it's looking at a `SnapshotDataObject`.
